$comment: §8 ratification record (resolution plan) — the four decision-maker sign-off points, answered by rvo on 2026-07-28 (AskUserQuestion in the Step-B build session; also recorded in PR #29's body). After this record the freeze applies: any change to a frozen artifact or the measurement surface (bound by frozenSurfaceDigest below, recomputed and enforced by the matrix/fidelity gate) invalidates affected timing data and requires a plan amendment plus one adversarial review round. The matrix (Step C) refuses to run unless this file is committed, all four answers are non-empty, noiseBand equals pilot.json's calibrated band, and the digest matches the working tree.

answers.noiseBandAndDominance: RATIFIED — noise band 1.25 (K=5 pilot of T0 on C2 at the frozen revision: walls 22360/22044/22590/22745/22793 ms, spread 1.034; the formula's floor binds) and §4.7's dominance definition (≥1 unit-win, 0 unit-losses against every eligible rival; within-band differences are ties).
answers.protocolConstants: RATIFIED — K=5; 2 GiB per-unit sampled-peak disk gate; G4 attributable-secondary-signal partition pass/warn/fail at 0/1/≥2; T1 caps (alias 250, query-doc 48 KiB, batch content 1.5 MiB, argv 128 KiB) and the full pinned failure policy (6-attempt total, TIMEOUT-type/pinned-regex + 2×{502,503,504}@≥80%-cap split triggers, split depth ≤2 with ≤4 descendants, breaker at 3 consecutive failed dispatches, REST fallback budget max(20, ceil(10%)) for every driver).
answers.corpusPinning: RATIFIED — the corpus as pinned with recorded verification evidence: C1 prometheus/prometheus ×4 branch units (88.6% shared blob oids best pair; the plan's fastify measured ≤14.2% and was swapped under the amended sharing-measure definition), C2 nestjs/nest (2,128 files, 51 manifests; undici measured 791 files and was swapped), C3 kubernetes/kubernetes (REST tree 37,393 entries, mean path 64.2 B, 21,461 at directory depth ≥6; T2a api-escapes here per the pinned threshold), C4 llvm/llvm-project (REST-truncated at the pin; 1,274 reads via the production clone-walk; oversized-and-truncated → T2a clones anyway, the exhibited hole), C5 PowerShell/PowerShell (measured autocrlf checkout divergence on selected files), C6 = M9 + ansible symlink + git/git non-UTF-8 (single-repo unification exhausted over all three candidates with per-candidate evidence recorded; the split stands per the amended §4.2 contingency) — INCLUDING C3/C4's natural workload sizes and their budget cost.
answers.symlinkPolicy: RATIFIED — REST-dereference parity with today's findings for every driver: mode-120000 entries resolve via the REST dereference fallback (counted against the universal fallback budget); T0 delivers the same dereferenced bytes as its status-quo primary; the canonical link payload stays a latent 2c capability, not a findings change.

amendments.why: A post-ratification review found the harness biased its own primary metric. The §4.6 disk sampler ran a synchronous recursive directory walk on the main thread INSIDE the measured wall, and two further walks sat between the driver's return and wall.stop(). Walk cost scales with entry count, so it taxed checkout-materialising runs (T2a on every unit EXCEPT the api-escaping C3; T0/T1 on the truncated-tree fallback) and barely touched T2c's --no-checkout store — a driver-correlated tax on exactly the axis under test. The §8 pilot could not have surfaced the DRIVER-CORRELATED part: T0-on-C2 creates no checkout, so its run directory stays small and the walk there is cheap — the pilot rows do record sampling (~1.6 MB peaks), so the cost was small, not zero. Fixed by moving the walk to a worker thread and taking the final snapshot with the wall paused (§4.6 items 1 and 4, both amended). This removes the main-thread BLOCKING. It does NOT remove all wall-time interference, because a walk on another thread still competes for CPU and disk bandwidth with the git subprocess under test. Reclamation stays inside the wall on the normal path, unchanged (see the R5 exception noted below).
alsoFixed: the §8 freeze gate trusted `git status --porcelain` without checking its exit code, so a status-specific failure yielded empty stdout and read as a clean tree — the tamper-detection leg failing OPEN

`git rev-parse HEAD` was unchecked and unvalidated, so a failure recorded harnessCommit:"" in every row and reduced the resume guard's revision check to "" !== "", silently merging rows from different harness revisions

the fidelity battery parsed `ls-tree` output without checking its exit code; the deadline path returns empty stdout, which parsed as 'entry absent from the live tree' and wrote a pass:false row — manufacturing a permanent, never-rerunnable driver disqualification (§4.7) from a transient local failure. Local tooling faults now raise a typed BenchOperationalError instead

pinning coerced an absent, opaque, or alias-errored GraphQL response into the positive fact isBinary:true, which deriveRoutes freezes as primary binary-fallback with no permitted alternative — a latent re-pin hazard that would disqualify T1 on an artifact of one flaky alias. Facts now commit per batch, only when every alias is sound

the mid-unit drift restart returned before teardown, leaking the run's sqlite handle and sidecars while its record claimed diskReclaimFailed:false; reclamation is now idempotent and owned by an outer finally that also covers the pre-driver throw paths. NOTE the R5 exception: that path stops the wall before the halt record is appended, so its reclamation happens in the outer finally OUTSIDE the stopped wall — §4.6.1's in-wall reclamation applies to the normal path

the R5 halt record summed httpBodyBytes without the rest-meta exclusion the normal record applies (contradicting an invariant the module states twice), hardcoded diskSamples:0, and zeroed traffic it had actually observed; both records now derive from one summarizeTraffic helper
buildEnvManifest ignored the exit codes of `git --version` and `gh --version`, so a blank version could enter the environment-manifest hash that binds every timed row

BatchChild.dispose()'s verdict — the fatal condition plus git's retained stderr — was discarded by every caller, so a poisoned teardown could accompany a reported success and the double-death message lost the first child's diagnosis
alsoFixedInReviewRound2: the frozen-surface digest walked scripts/ NON-recursively, silently omitting all eight tracked non-test modules under scripts/tui/ — a freeze that covered less than its own description claimed. The traversal is now recursive, which is why the digest differs from the one first recorded for this amendment

the worker-backed disk sampler had no error channel, no reply deadline, and no idempotence, so a worker that died or never replied would hang between the driver returning and the run record being appended; instrumentation failure now degrades the disk fields (cloneObjectStoreBytes null, diskSampleError set) and never eats the row, which also restores R5's before-any-fallible-work guarantee
cloneObjectStoreBytes was computed with the deliberately-tolerant sampling walker, so an unreadable object store could report a plausible 0 — it is a measurement, so a failed walk is now null
parseProbeBatch accepted arrays and non-Blob nodes and coerced absent fields into definite facts; it now requires __typename Blob with correctly-typed fields

BatchChild disposal was only rejected on an explicit protocol fault, and the fidelity path discarded the verdict entirely; the FINAL successful-path disposal in runT2c and the fidelity disposal now both require exit 0 with no fault. SCOPE: the first child's disposal on the respawn path is captured for diagnostics and is NOT itself gated — a replacement child that succeeds still yields a successful run.
alsoFixedInReviewRound3: the round-2 entry above claimed cloneObjectStoreBytes failures became null; that claim was PREMATURE. The wrapper caught throws, but the walker underneath was still the tolerant duBytes, which returns 0 and never throws — so the catch was unreachable and a missing store still recorded a plausible 0. All three reviewers reproduced it independently. There is now a genuinely strict walker (duBytesStrict) that raises on any unreadable entry, selected per-request so sampled peaks stay tolerant and the recorded measurement does not
the worker's inbound request was cast rather than validated, and reply sequence numbers accepted fractional/negative values; both are now parsed and rejected

concurrent finish() calls raced through one worker — the first terminated it and cleared the second's pending entry without rejecting it. finish() is now single-flight: the in-progress promise is stored before the first await
the awaited walk's deadline timer was unref'd, so a worker terminated mid-finish could let the process exit 0 with no snapshot and no run row; it is now referenced for the life of the request

pilot.json was READ by the freeze gate but excluded from the digest, so its walls, spread, reps, driver, or slot could be edited freely as long as noiseBand still matched. It is now inside the frozen artifact set
diskSampleError was write-only: nothing logged or acted on it, so a degraded disk row could later read as a real measurement. It now emits an explicit operator warning naming the affected row
runT2c's exception path assigned the disposal verdict in its finally and then skipped the check, discarding the diagnosis exactly as before; an unclean teardown now annotates the propagating error
alsoFixedInReviewRound4: the R5 halt path peeked the sampler and threw without ever releasing it — finish() is the only other disposer and that path deliberately never calls it, so the tick timer stayed armed and the worker outlived the run. A synchronous, infallible, idempotent abandon() now runs immediately after the row is durable

the runT2c exception-path teardown annotation was written to Error.message, but the engine records UnitFailure.cause2 — so the disposal diagnosis was preserved in a field nothing reads and remained absent from runs.jsonl. UnitFailure now exposes annotateTeardown(), which updates cause2 (and keeps message consistent)

the T1 fidelity path mapped an http-failure analysis (5xx / no HTTP response / non-JSON body — all TRANSIENT) to route 'unresolved:http-failure' and appended a pass:false row, manufacturing a permanent never-rerunnable driver disqualification from a transport blip. This is the third instance of that defect class found in this harness; it now raises BenchOperationalError like the ls-tree path
amendments.note: The four §8 sign-off answers below are untouched and remain as rvo recorded them on 2026-07-28. This amendment changes the measurement surface, not the decisions: the noise band, protocol constants, corpus pinning, and symlink policy are all unaffected. No timed matrix data existed to invalidate — the matrix has never run.
amendments.reaffirmation: NOT gate-enforced, and deliberately so: the matrix gate checks the digest, not who approved it, so updating frozenSurfaceDigest above is sufficient to let Step C run. The decision-maker should nevertheless re-affirm this amended surface before executing the matrix; that judgement is recorded here rather than mechanised, and no field in this file is checked for it.
alsoFixedInReviewRound5: FOURTH and FIFTH instances of the transient-failure-becomes-permanent-verdict class. The T1 fidelity path routed only http-failure to an operational error; GraphQL TIMEOUT (batch or per-alias), throttle-retry, and the closed default still fell through to route 'unresolved:*' and appended pass:false, disqualifying the driver globally. That branch is now an ELSE — anything that is not one of the delivering cases fails closed, so a NEW analysis kind cannot reopen the hole

analyzeBatchResponse ignored `gh`'s exit code entirely, so a subprocess that FAILED but emitted a parseable 200-shaped body produced resolved aliases — content accepted from a call that did not succeed. A non-zero exit is now an http-failure before any body inspection

runT2c swallowed a REJECTED dispose(): the catch set finalDisposal = null, which the post-teardown check reads as 'nothing to complain about', so a teardown that failed outright returned a clean run. A rejection is now its own unclean verdict on both the success and exception paths
the R5 sampler release ran AFTER runsLog.append, so an appendFileSync failure (disk full, EACCES) left the sampler armed with no disposer remaining; abandon() now runs in a finally around the append

WorkerDiskSampler folded ANY well-shaped reply with an unrecognised sequence into the peak as 'an unawaited tick', so a duplicate, stale, or unsolicited message could fabricate a disk figure the filesystem never held. Exactly one outstanding tick sequence is now tracked and anything else fails the sampler

a throw in post-run finalisation (the rate-limit read) between reclamation and the append discarded a run that had already been measured — wall, traffic and all. It now appends an 'invalidated-finalisation' row preserving the measured wall and partial traffic, marked unscoreable rather than dropped
alsoFixedInReviewRound6: abandon() cleared the pending map without settling it. Because the awaited walk's deadline timers are deliberately REFERENCED (so a dead worker cannot let the process exit mid-measurement), dropping them unsettled left those timers holding the event loop. abandon() now rejects every pending request
the worker's request validator used extras.some(), which SKIPS array holes, so a sparse array passed and was then cast to string[]

GET /user was cast to {login?:string} with a `?? "unknown"` fallback, so a malformed payload silently became the literal identity "unknown" — which then hashes into the §8 environment manifest that every timed row binds to. It is now validated and refuses

openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.finding: A git spawn TIMEOUT (exit 124 — clone, scaffolding fetch, or ls-tree) is thrown as UnitFailure with no HTTP evidence, so the engine records failureEvidence {kind:'unit'} and the matrix rerun predicate (isRerunnable, benchContentTransport.ts) refuses it: it accepts only {kind:'http'}. A transient transport timeout therefore becomes a permanent, non-rerunnable unit failure — a sixth instance of the transient-becomes-permanent class found in this harness.
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.CORRECTION: An earlier version of this entry claimed the fix was blocked because '§4.5's R1/R2 rerun predicate and the failure policy are covered by ratified answer 2'. THAT WAS FALSE, and the prose audit caught it. Ratified answer 2 covers 'K=5, the 2 GiB per-unit disk gate, the G4 secondary-limit threshold, and the fixed T1 caps and failure-policy CONSTANTS (§4.4)'. R1/R2 is a separate §4.5 completion-discipline definition and is NOT one of the four ratified answers. The reason given for deferring was wrong, and it is recorded here rather than silently replaced because a false justification for NOT doing work is worse than the omission it excused.
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.actualStatus: Fixing this is a §4.5 PLAN AMENDMENT of exactly the same kind as the §4.6 amendments already made in this remediation — not a change to any ratified answer. It is deferred only because the adversarial review loop that would validate it has just run five rounds and closed; introducing an unreviewed change to the rerun predicate now would reintroduce the risk that loop exists to manage. Three of those five rounds found defects introduced while fixing the previous round's.
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.recommendedFix: Add a typed {kind:'spawn', timedOut:true, op:'clone'|'fetch'|'ls-tree'} failureEvidence variant from BenchGitResult.timedOut, PRESERVING WHICH OPERATION STALLED, and admit only the network-facing ones in isRerunnable alongside R1's no-response case. SCOPE CAVEAT (raised by the prose audit): §4.5's R1 covers 'a network-layer error outside any HTTP response'. A clone/fetch timeout plausibly qualifies; an ls-tree timeout is a purely LOCAL operation and does not, and a process-level timeout does not by itself prove which phase stalled. The amendment must therefore either preserve the phase and admit only the network-facing subset, or explicitly broaden R1 to cover local tooling stalls — an earlier draft of this entry recommended admitting all spawn timeouts, which would have over-broadened R1.

harnessCommit: informational only — the digest above is the binding, and each row in runs.jsonl records the commit that produced it. Pre-rebase hashes recorded earlier (e.g. 42c970f) are not ancestors of the current branch.
environmentNote: All timed matrix data must come from ONE machine/network/credential (§8): the matrix gate requires an explicit BENCH_NETWORK_DESC and stamps the environment manifest hash into every row; resume refuses rows from any other harness commit or environment hash. The pilot + pinning ran under gh login sondrateconsulting-ryan; §4.8's dedicated-otherwise-idle identity requirement for the matrix stands (a foreign single-point GraphQL consumption was live-detected and R3-invalidated during pilot rework — the requirement is not theoretical).
adversarialReviewRecord: gpt-5.6-sol @ ultra, four rounds during the ORIGINAL Step-B build (pre-rebase hashes R1 dddcb37 / R2 8e8eb6d / R3 48b47a8 / R4 42c970f are ancestors of the pre-rebase branch, not of current HEAD). AFTER ratification this branch was remediated across six commits (d60603c, then santa-loop rounds 1-5: c982684, d07f980, f83db0a, 9412fec, e87e173), reviewed by a three-model adversarial loop (Claude Opus 4.6 @ xhigh, GPT-5.5 @ xhigh, GPT-5.6 Sol @ ultra). That loop did NOT reach unanimous approval: rounds 1-4 each returned at least one FAIL, and the residual items are recorded in openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed above and in the PR body. The R5-record items previously carried into Step C are now FIXED (see alsoFixed / alsoFixedInReviewRound2..6), not deferred.
pilotProvenance: The K=5 pilot rows in runs.jsonl were produced at pre-rebase harness revisions (22b7152 / 8e8eb6d), BEFORE the post-ratification remediation changed measurement behaviour. The gate binds the ratified band to pilot.json's band and the surface to the digest; it does NOT bind the pilot rows to the frozen revision. The pilot configuration (T0 on C2) materialises no checkout, so the disk-sampler bias the remediation removed was ~0 there and the 1.034 spread is not expected to move — but that is an argument, NOT a measurement on the current surface. Treat 'the noise band is unaffected' as reasoned, not verified. Re-running the pilot at the frozen revision before Step C would settle it.
